neighbours.label: concessive 'though' / 'although' opening a mid-sentence clause after a comma
fire: The house, though small, had a lovely garden.
His speech, although brief, moved the crowd.
The film, though long, never felt slow.
Our team, although tired, kept attacking.
The road, though narrow, was well paved.
The soup, although cold, tasted wonderful.
The plan, though risky, was approved by the board.
Her answer, although polite, was clearly a refusal.
quiet: The house, being small, had only one garden.
His speech, as usual, moved the crowd.
The film, at three hours, never felt slow.
Our team, when tired, kept attacking.
The road, once narrow, was now well paved.
The soup, served cold, tasted wonderful.
The plan, after review, was approved by the board.
Her answer, as expected, was clearly a refusal.

notes: Card: ' whether' x6, ' though' x5, ' although' x4, Spanish aunque, Chinese 由/因. Probe: ', though short,' 0.64, ', although slow,' 0.50, ', because' 0.18, sentence-final though 0.03, whether 0.01.
